context: Sakura interviews a young pastry chef for an article over coffee.
purpose: Writer interviewing young culinary craftsman warmly.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: パン作り、何年されてますか?
lines.en: How long have you been baking bread?
lines.style: Warm, curious opening. Pen poised as if taking notes. Genuinely interested — the kind of interviewer who listens more than she speaks. Soft eye contact.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 七年です、まだ修行中で。
lines.en: Seven years now. Still learning, really.
lines.style: Quiet, modest. A small self-deprecating smile underneath. Not fishing for reassurance — just stating fact. Gentle down-turn at the end.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.en: Do you have any particular methods you care about?
lines.style: Leaning in slightly. Pen ready. The follow-up question of someone who's listening carefully, not just moving down a checklist. Warm curiosity.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 酵母、自家製にしています。
lines.style: A quiet note of pride underneath the softness. Simple statement, but the kind that matters. Slight lift on the word 'own' — this is the detail he wanted to share.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.style: Genuine admiration — not performing it. She means it. Warm recognition of something that takes patience. Nods slightly as she writes.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 時間かかるけど、味が違う。
lines.en: It takes time, but the flavor is completely different.
lines.style: Settling into the topic. Content, unhurried. Not defensive about the time investment — simply stating what he knows. Soft warmth in the delivery.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.en: Your readers are going to love that detail.
lines.style: Professional warmth. She can already see how this will land on the page. Slight smile — the satisfaction of a writer who knows a good story when she's hearing one.
